p030-032.name: Part 1's intro line with the Metabolic Red Line's first paragraph, fixed for sense from their reads
p030-032.text:
To see what each tool in this protocol does, let's look first at what goes wrong in the brain under trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress, since those "Hardware Failures" are what it's built to fix.

If you've tried to talk yourself out of a trigger and couldn't, it's because blood flow in your brain shifts away from the Cortex, which handles logic and reasoning, toward the Brainstem, the part that keeps you alive. That happens once your heart rate climbs above its usual resting rate, or its variability drops (a smartwatch shows both), and it lasts until you calm down. Perry describes the point where that happens as a "Metabolic Red Line" for the traumatized brain, and calls the state past it "Fear".
p030-032.diagnosis: the intro line opened on a rule ("you must understand ... before applying the tools") before why, with "Hardware Failures" hung on as a label; the Red Line paragraph had two abstract nouns acting ("anatomy overrides intellect"), Perry and his term before the reader, a packed sentence with glosses built alike, and no line past which; the stretch with them read Human (#134) and the paragraph alone Human Medium (#130)
p030-032.decides: whether the intro line, under 50 words, reads Human High with the paragraph it leads into, after the sense fixes
p030-032.tells: a list of three in the intro (trauma, withdrawal or chronic stress: the protocol's scope); a long condition before the point in the second sentence of the paragraph
p030-032.human_tells: none to name: the words are mine and the post's
p030-032.first_fix: payoff: the intro opens on what the reader gets (what each tool does), the paragraph on the reader's own failure and what happens while triggered; join: the label tied into the intro's sentence ("since those Hardware Failures are what it's built to fix"); plain: "the part of your brain that reasons goes offline" for "anatomy overrides intellect", "above its usual resting rate" for "your resting heart rate goes up"
p030-032.humanized: the intro opens on what the reader gets ("To see what each tool in this protocol does"), the reader inside it ("let's look first"), its label tied in as what the protocol fixes; and the paragraph after it: the reason the reader asks for comes straight after their own failure, in the same sentence ("it's because blood flow in your brain shifts"); when it happens and that it passes, tied on with "That happens"; the Cortex and the Brainstem each explained where first used, the two glosses built differently; Perry's names last, once the reader has the thing they name; plain words for the abstract ones ("the part that keeps you alive" for "runs survival")

p033.name: The Metabolic Red Line's second paragraph by itself, fixed for sense from its reads
p033.text: So if you try to process trauma while you're above this red line, you're adding to the armor instead of taking it off. Above the line your functional IQ drops a lot, and stress chemicals called catecholamines flood the Nucleus Accumbens, a reward center deep in the brain. There they set off the making of DeltaFosB, a protein that may be what holds the armor in place, though the research on that isn't settled. Only work on your trauma while you're under that line, which trauma therapists call staying in your "window of tolerance".
p033.diagnosis: never checked as it stands (his 39a moved the window of tolerance and the DeltaFosB caveat in after #134); the reads: the advice before the mechanism, "In that state" read as inside the window, "many trauma therapies" before the reader, "rather than overwhelming activation" a contrast nobody needs, catecholamines said to "transcribe" proteins, DeltaFosB both "the armor itself" and "the master switch"
